title: Phase 0 context-economy measurement: do fan-out fixed overhead and retries dominate amplification?
summary: Hypothesis: per-worker input-token amplification in orchestrator runs is dominated by fixed fan-out overhead (each worker re-reading the same prompt scaffold and context) and by retries/checkpoint resumes, rather than by task-specific work. Method: ran the deterministic, privacy-safe `agent-os orchestrate context-economy` harness read-only over .agent-local/orchestrator/runs (20 runs, 653 exact-usage calls), reporting aggregates only (no prompt or transcript text). Outcome: inconclusive. The model-based fan-out overhead estimate is 253.4M of 255.8M worker input tokens (share 0.9905); this is an upper bound that does not separate the fixed per-worker scaffold from repeated re-reads of context within a worker, so it does not show how much is task-specific. Pooled amplification is 104.8x and the median worker role (implementer/repairer/test_author) sees 141-189x, while reviewers sit at 11.7x. Retries/repeat attempts account for 47.7M tokens (about 19% of worker input; 26 retries, 63 escalations, 15 fallbacks) and checkpoint-resume overhead is 17.2% of run input in the runs that resumed, so retries and resumes are material but secondary. Long sessions do not enlarge later calls (per-node last/first input median 0.78 and 0.43) but cumulative input per run grows superlinearly in most runs (exponent up to 1.88). Interpretation: most input is cache reads (median cache-read share 0.84). Whether trimming scaffold size and worker count is the main lever, versus reducing in-worker re-reads, is a Phase 1 hypothesis that this data cannot settle. Caveat: the overhead share is a model-based upper bound and the amplification denominator is a characters/4 estimate. See EVR-0018.
